verevonRelevance: Verevon execution-core risk classification is a substring list that can mis-class names; AST-based command analysis closes that gap for any future shell tool (baseline: findings/t3/v-modelplane.baseline.md).

name: Smart mode: LLM auto-review classifier for risky actions
what: An auto-review model classifies pending shell, MCP, web fetch and computer actions as allow or block using user-written instructions, optionally in shadow mode.
how: tj classifier gets action kind (shell, mcp, sand_computer, web_fetch, fetch_mcp_resource), the target arguments and execution surface (host_machine or isolated_box), a 10 s timeout and 2 attempts; permissions.json autoRun/autoReview supplies allow_instructions and block_instructions as natural language; shadow mode classifies without enforcing; not used for background agents; a block returns a system reminder telling the agent it may retry with requestSmartModeApproval and smartModeBlockReason to raise a native approval card; the shell classifier also suggests allowlist entries.
verevonRelevance: Natural-language policy instructions evaluated by a model, with shadow mode for rollout and a user-approval escape hatch, suit Verevon org-level agent policies; keep deterministic checks first.

name: Admin command denylist, team blocklist and delete protection
what: Organizations can hard-block commands and protect against file deletion regardless of user settings.
how: adminCommandDenylist flows through request context into ShellArgs and is enforced at execution time as a hard block (with parser-failure handling); team auto-run controls provide allowlist and blocklist; getDeleteFileProtection makes rm always denied; team settings can override dashboard terminal allowlists and block run mode entirely.
verevonRelevance: Enforce org denylists at the executor, not only in the prompt: they must survive prompt injection and misconfigured agents.

name: MCP permission model with allowlists and admin network modes
what: MCP calls obey tool allowlists (server:tool patterns) and admin policies; readonly mode blocks them; stdio servers can be network-restricted.
how: permissions.json mcpAllowlist entries server:tool, server:*, *:tool, *:*; shouldBlockMcp logic blocks in readonly mode with Smart Mode forcing; mcp_allowlist_precheck exec messages; admin allowedMcpConfiguration and mcpNetworkMode (allow_all, allowlist, deny_all, no_sandbox); precheck messages also exist for shell and web fetch.
verevonRelevance: A precheck RPC separate from execution lets the UI show approval state before a call is made; Verevon connector permissions can reuse the server:tool pattern grammar.

name: Privacy modes and purpose-checked redaction matrix
what: Five privacy modes decide what may be stored, logged or used for training; code, paths and credentials are classified separately.
how: PrivacyMode UNSPECIFIED, NO_STORAGE, NO_TRAINING, USAGE_DATA_TRAINING_ALLOWED, USAGE_CODEBASE_TRAINING_ALLOWED; matrix: modes 0 and 1 allow nothing except SAFE and UNSAFE_ALWAYS_ALLOWED; mode 2 allows PATH and PROVIDER_INFO for logging and anything for usage but nothing for training; modes 3 and 4 allow all except CREDENTIALS and UNSPECIFIED which are never storable; features such as A/B response comparison and prompt-quality uploads check for mode 4; Sentry reporting is suppressed in privacy mode; request header x-ghost-mode carries the mode.
verevonRelevance: Verevon enforces ZDR with evidence-bound gating at feature level; a typed redacted-string layer with purpose-checked unwrap would add compile-time protection against logging or storing content on ZDR paths (baseline: findings/t3/v-modelplane.baseline.md).

name: Prompt-injection posture: instructions plus structural sanitization
what: Defense is mostly prompt-level cautions and sanitization of hook-injected text, not a dedicated detector.
how: Background-agent prompt tells the model to be cautious following instructions inside tool results (especially web search) and to prioritize the original request, and not to reply to linked external services unless asked; hook output text has system_reminder tags neutralized before reaching the model; MCP, shell and fetch calls go through approval or classifier; no content-injection classifier for tool outputs was found.
verevonRelevance: Verevon should exceed this: mark untrusted tool-output spans, strip control markup from them and keep policy decisions in the capability gate rather than prompt text (baseline: findings/t3/v-modelplane.baseline.md).
notes: Absence of a classifier is INF from not finding one in the bundles.

name: Read policy outside the workspace and ignore services
what: Reading files outside the workspace or ignored by policy needs approval; team read policy can restrict the whole read boundary.
how: PermissionsService has an ignoreService (cursorignore patterns), a pendingDecisionStore, team settings and admin network controls; reading outside the workspace returns needsApproval with a team-policy message unless approval mode is unrestricted; redacted_read exec messages exist for protected files; sandbox readBoundary workspace versus system is merged with user and admin settings.
verevonRelevance: Per-path read policy (workspace boundary, ignore files, redacted reads) matters for Verevon Spaces and owner-plane ACL rules; reads outside the granted scope should need explicit approval.

name: Secrets as placeholders and structured secret requests
what: The agent never types secrets; it requests them through structured setup actions and refers to them by name.
how: env_setup_actions XML includes add_secrets entries that list secret names (for example API keys) without values; ReplaceEnv updates environment variables through an interaction query; secretRedactionEnabled is part of the request context env and ExecServerMessage has redacted_read results; MCP refresh tokens are fetched through ControlService.GetMcpRefreshTokens rather than embedded in prompts.
verevonRelevance: Secrets should be named handles resolved by the sandbox runtime; Verevon connectors must never put token values in prompts.

name: Per-request TTFT breakdown sent to the client
what: Latency to first token is decomposed into server and client stages and returned with the stream.
how: AgentServerMessage.ttft_breakdown carries server_first_token_ms, pre_stream_setup_ms, wait_for_first_event_ms, provider_ttft_ms and slow_pool_wait_ms; client-side agent.ttft.* metrics cover conversation init, blob hydration, context enrichment (blob store, documentation, external links), middleware chain, system prompt generation, user message blob, state snapshot and first step setup.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has SLO harnesses (mp-slo) offline only; per-request stage timing in the stream would give live latency attribution in agent pages (baseline: findings/t3/v-modelplane.baseline.md).

name: Prompt token breakdown and context usage API
what: The runtime estimates tokens per prompt category and exposes context usage for UI display.
how: Metric agent.prompt_token_breakdown.category_estimated_tokens; trackPromptTokens; AgentService.GetPromptContextUsage; ChatService.GetPromptDryRun returns the exact prompt; flags context_visualizer and context_usage_canvas.
verevonRelevance: A prompt dry-run and per-category token accounting make agents explainable; Verevon pages should offer a context inspector.

name: Trace-level RPC logging in the host with privacy-aware truncation
what: The agent host can trace every RPC and stream event as JSON with long strings truncated.
how: When trace is enabled the host logs each RPC (toJson), stream events (event case, value, eventId) and createSession parameters, truncating strings above 2048 chars; a privacy log channel routes logs; the extensions request the cursorTracing proposed API; settings cursor.rpcFileLogger.* and cursor-rpc-devtools exist.
verevonRelevance: A per-session trace of typed events (with truncation) is an easy and valuable debugging surface for Model Plane runs.

name: Tool-call telemetry with owner team labels and arg-size histograms
what: Each tool call is measured by name, outcome, owner team, client type and whether the tool is dynamic.
how: tool_call.duration_ms and tool_call.result carry labels toolName, outcome, team, mcp_version, clientversion, clienttype, remoteType, isdynamic, user.is_dev; argument size histograms estimate tokens as length/4; per-tool metrics for read, str_replace, edit_common perform_edit/perform_write, generate_image, mcp meta.
verevonRelevance: Same labeling scheme is recommended for Verevon tool metrics.

name: Hook execution tracking and response comparison feedback surfaces
what: Hooks and feedback prompts are observable events, not hidden side effects.
how: trackHookExecuted records hook step, source (local or remote), type, status (success, blocked, failed, timeout), latency and failClosed; hook state files live under .cursor/hooks/state; feedback_request updates carry categories and category groups for in-line feedback; customize_hooks_execution_log_detail flag.
verevonRelevance: Hook outcomes must be visible in the run trace so admins can debug policy behaviour.

name: NDJSON log ingest server for agent-driven debugging
what: A local HTTP server receives NDJSON logs from instrumented user code and writes them where the agent can read them.
how: cursor-ndjson-ingest (5 commands; settings ndjson.port in 7242-7942 and ndjson.bindAddress with a warning for non-localhost) writes workspace/.cursor/debug.log; the Debug mode prompt tells the agent to POST there or append to the file.
verevonRelevance: A tiny log sink makes runtime evidence available to agents without attaching a debugger.

name: Model family detection driving prompt variants and toolsets
what: The harness derives vendor and family flags from the model slug and picks prompts, tool descriptions and edit tools accordingly.
how: mde(slug) lowercases and substring-matches into flags (isSonnet45, isGemini3, isGpt51, isGpt52, isGpt54, isGpt55, isCodexFamily, isGpt53Codex, isClaude4X, isOpus45/46/48, isOpus5, isGpt5Family, isComposer1/15/2, isComposerMatterhorn, isRawTrainingSlug); Cursor models map to promptVersion dsv3-1018, dsv3-1205 or cursor-0226 (matterhorn and composer-2 use cursor-0226), everything else uses latest; system prompt components branch on these flags (for example the identity line, citing code, inline line numbers only for GPT-5 family).
verevonRelevance: Verevon routes across Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere and OpenAI-compatible endpoints; a model profile record (prompt variant, edit toolset, reasoning options) beats slug matching (baseline: findings/t3/v-modelplane.baseline.md).
notes: String-matching on slugs is brittle; treat it as the anti-pattern to avoid.

name: Anthropic prompt caching with rolling cache-control markers
what: Prompt caching is managed by the harness: the last message always gets an ephemeral cache marker and older markers roll off at a block limit.
how: A message-list wrapper applies cacheControl ephemeral to the last message and trims to maxCacheBlocks (4), removing cacheControl from older messages; the provider shim maps cacheControl to cache_control on text, image, document and tool_result blocks; cache read and write tokens are tracked in usage and summarization metrics.
verevonRelevance: Verevon supports Anthropic-native clear_tool_uses optionally; explicit rolling cache breakpoints with read/write token accounting should be a default for Anthropic routes (baseline: findings/t3/v-modelplane.baseline.md).

name: Executor middleware chain around the model call
what: Model calls pass through composable middleware that fix up messages and add tracing.
how: An executor base class wraps an inner executor (getMessages, appendMessages, clearMessages, stream); middleware include continuation-injector (adds a continuation user message after a trailing assistant), trailing-empty-assistant-removal, image-resizing and effort-level (present as stubs in this build); a tracing middleware records agent.ttft.middlewareChainMs and chat_inference.* metrics; providers (Anthropic, OpenAI) are executed through a vendored Vercel AI SDK streamText.
verevonRelevance: A decorator chain over a ModelExecutor trait is the idiomatic Rust structure for provider quirks (empty assistant messages, continuation, image limits).
notes: effort-level and image-resizing middleware appear as logger stubs here; real behaviour may live server-side.

name: Reasoning block preservation and model-switch handling
what: Reasoning text, signatures and redacted reasoning are preserved across turns, and the model is warned when earlier turns came from a different model.
how: The stream accumulator keeps reasoning, reasoning-signature and redacted-reasoning chunks with providerOptions.cursor.modelName; summarized thinking is flagged; on a model change a system reminder tells the model that earlier turns were produced by a different AI model, may have used tools no longer available, and that it must call only currently defined tools with current schemas.
verevonRelevance: Verevon lacks reasoning-effort control on the OpenAI/Azure route and has no Gemini or native DeepSeek provider; preserving reasoning blocks with model provenance is needed before adding them (baseline: findings/t3/v-modelplane.baseline.md).

name: Usable-model, model-intent and routed-model APIs
what: The client asks the backend which models and intents are allowed and is told which model auto-routing chose.
how: AgentService.GetUsableModels, GetDefaultModelForCli, GetAllowedModelIntents and new-chat nudges for the model picker; InteractionUpdate.routed_model reports the chosen model; AgentRunRequest carries requested_model, model_details and selected_subagent_models; admin blockedModels and byokDisabled settings.
verevonRelevance: Return the effective routed model in the stream so pages can show it; allowed-model lists should come from org policy.

name: Specialist perception subagents on specific models (video)
what: A coding agent without video understanding delegates to a subagent running a video-capable model that acts as its eyes.
how: watchVideo and mediaReview subagents (models limited to Gemini variants) with a long role prompt describing the agent as having no ability to watch videos; flags gemini_video_developer_api, enable_watch_video_in_ide and agent_video_signed_url_uploads; GetSignedUrlForAttachedMedia RPC for media upload.
verevonRelevance: Perception as a subagent on a different provider is a clean way to add video or audio to any Verevon model without changing the main loop.

name: Warm-up and prewarm to cut time to first token
what: The client can warm the backend while the user is still typing.
how: AgentClientMessage.prewarm_request mirrors the run request without an action; ChatService has WarmStreamUnifiedChatWithTools and WarmFullFileCmdK; FastApplyService.WarmApply; ShadowWorkspace and VmDaemon warm calls (WarmCursorServer, WarmRemoteAccessServer).
verevonRelevance: Prewarm (provider connection, cache priming) when the user focuses the composer is a cheap latency win for Verevon chat.

name: Continual learning by transcript search, not an automatic memory store
what: Agents are told to recognize preferences and corrections and to ask whether they should apply globally; past conversations are searched by a subagent.
how: continual_learning prompt section for cloud agents: a past_conversation_explorer subagent searches earlier transcripts; the model should notice preferences, corrections, tips and codebase knowledge, and clarify global versus local scope; agent transcripts are stored as JSONL files in agent-transcripts; no automatic memory writer was found for cloud agents.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already has Letta memory and Dreaming extraction (ahead of Cursor here); copy only the explicit global-versus-local scope question and transcript search tool (baseline: findings/t3/v-modelplane.baseline.md).
notes: Absence of an automatic store is INF from bundle search.

name: Persistent agent identity files and agent stores
what: Named agents keep durable files for identity and memory and sync them between environments.
how: Home store /cursor/stores/home with SELF.md (identity, embedded in user_info via an agent_self_document block with tag escaping), SOUL.md and an activity folder; agent store mounts with a principal alias; agent-store-sync keeps local and cloud copies consistent; AgentStoreService is part of the Grok Bot service set.
verevonRelevance: File-based identity and memory is simple, inspectable and syncable; map to Verevon per-user memory documents in the Data Plane.

name: Conversation search tool for the agent
what: The agent can search past conversations with a tool backed by the local FTS index.
how: SearchConversations tool (exec message conversation_search_args/result) backed by the conversation search process; flags agent_conversation_search_tool and local_agent_transcript_search_in_glass; subagent type pastConversationExplorer.
verevonRelevance: Chat history as a searchable tool for agents is cheap personalization; scope it by space and ACL in Verevon.

name: Automation memories
what: Scheduled automations keep their own memories that can be listed and edited.
how: AutomationsService ListAutomationMemories, GetAutomationMemory, UpdateAutomationMemory, DeleteAutomationMemory; a memory-instructions placeholder is substituted into automation prompts.
verevonRelevance: Per-automation memory as an editable object keeps long-running scheduled agents consistent.

name: Agent-authored interactive canvases (React TSX) with a host SDK
what: The agent can create interactive visual pages as TSX canvas files that render in the host with themed components and charts, and share them as artifacts.
how:
Canvases live at .cursor/projects/

/canvases/*.canvas.tsx; a canvas-server-provider compiles them (esbuild-wasm) after each edit with TypeScript diagnostics (jsx react-jsx, strict) fed back to the agent (canvas_diagnostics_args); sharing calls cursor.shareCanvasArtifact({title, visibility, appJs, dataJson, canvasPath}); the bundled SDK cursor/canvas offers Card, Grid, Row, Stack, Table, Stat, Callout, Pill, Code, Button, BarChart, LineChart, PieChart, DiffView, DiffStats, computeDAGLayout, TodoList, UsageBar, form primitives and hooks useHostTheme, useCanvasState, useCanvasAction; design rules are delivered through a built-in canvas skill.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has artifacts and canvas in the gateway loop; a typed component SDK and compile-diagnose loop would raise artifact quality and safety (baseline: findings/t3/v-modelplane.baseline.md).

name: Prompt suggestions, post-request prompts and shareable agent links
what: After a run the UI can show suggested next prompts, and agent sessions can be shared by link.
how: InteractionUpdate includes prompt_suggestion, post_request_prompt and user_message_appended; aiserver CreateAgentShare returns share_id and share_url and GetAgentSharePreview can include a preview image; flag cloud_glass_shared_sessions.
verevonRelevance: Server-generated follow-up prompts and share links are common chat features; keep them in the stream contract as typed updates.

name: Markdown output rules: inline images, preview cards and citations
what: The chat renders images inline from file paths and URLs and shows a Preview card when a local app is running; code citation formats are model-specific.
how: Prompt bullets (flag-gated) tell the model that the chat UI renders images via markdown with absolute local paths or URLs and that a preview tag on its own line shows a Preview card; citing_code section defines CODE REFERENCES versus MARKDOWN CODE BLOCKS for GPT-5-family; terminal output files are cited by path rather than described.
verevonRelevance: Server-side rules for what the UI can render (images, preview, code references) should be derived from a UI capability list sent by the page.

name: Image generation tool with concurrency limiter and abuse guards
what: The agent can generate images; calls are rate-limited per run and screened.
how: GenerateImage tool with a concurrency limiter (2), a suspicious-keywords check, restriction by model, mode gating (Ask mode) and metrics for execute duration, errors, render finished and short prompts; results are written to files and rendered inline.
verevonRelevance: Per-run concurrency limits and abuse keyword screens belong in the Model Plane tool layer for Verevon image creation.

name: Web search and fetch tools with hooks and allowlist precheck
what: Web search and fetch run through the same hook, permission and classifier pipeline as shell and MCP.
how: WebSearch and WebFetch tools (fetch enabled by availability and user setting), execute-hook integration (enableExecuteHookExec, configuredSteps), web_fetch_allowlist_precheck exec messages, smart-mode classification for web_fetch, and InteractionQuery.web_search and web_fetch for client-side execution.
verevonRelevance: Treat web access as a governed tool with allowlist prechecks; in Verevon this call should be executed by Quarry, not the model runtime.

name: Agent-first Glass window and UI intents
what: A separate agent-first window (Glass) hosts cloud projects, diff tabs and side chats beside the classic editor.
how: out/vs/workbench/workbench.glass.main.js renders the agent window with 111 glass_* flags (sidebar, projects, diffs, PDF, video, themes); the same runtime and services are reused; simulated message reasons wire diff-tab buttons to agent turns.
verevonRelevance: A dedicated agent surface separate from the code editor validates the Verevon direction (agent pages not an IDE); the shared runtime keeps both surfaces consistent.

name: System prompt as a JSX component tree with named sections and per-model gating
what: The system prompt is not a template string: it is a tree of components (System, User, Assistant, Tool, section) rendered to chat messages, with sections switched on by model family, agent type, mode and flags.
how: A tiny JSX-style renderer (EO/TO element constructors, class xO.renderToMessages/renderElement/renderIntrinsicElement) turns an element tree into role messages; sections render as XML-like tags (section title becomes the tag). Sections seen: task_management, tool_calling, making_code_changes, plan_mode_guardrails, tone_and_style, citing_code, maximize_context_understanding, semantic_search_instructions, browser_tools, inline_line_numbers, terminal_files_information, mode_selection, debug_mode_logging, continual_learning, background_agent, git_and_submission, testing, markdown_spec, status_update_spec, summary_spec, grep_spec, todo_spec, linter_errors, plus reducedSystemPrompt variants; the identity line even changes wording per model (agent versus assistant).
verevonRelevance: Composable prompt components with typed props (mode, toolInfo, modelInfo, flags) are testable and diffable; in Rust use an enum tree rendered by a PromptBuilder per model profile and snapshot-test the output.

name: Per-step system prompt generation and a persisted user_info snapshot with staleness check
what: The system prompt is regenerated each step, but the large first user message (user_info) is persisted and only re-rendered when something relevant changed, which keeps the prompt prefix cache-stable.
how: Each step unshifts a system message from systemPromptGenerator({requestContext, cursorRules, env, browserTools, cloudRule, mode,...}); the first user message contains a user_info block (OS, shell, workspace paths, git state, date, terminals folder, mounted stores, rules catalog, skills catalog, subagent models and types, MCP servers); shouldRerenderUserInfo re-renders it only if the agent type changed from persisted state, the available subagent models or types description changed, or the MCP meta-tool options changed; request-context completeness and a summarization epoch are stored in the message providerOptions.
verevonRelevance: Verevon Do mode starts with a fresh history and no persona, org or Space instructions; a persisted environment and instruction snapshot with explicit invalidation fixes seeding and improves cache hits (baseline: findings/t3/v-modelplane.baseline.md).

name: Per-turn tagged context blocks (attachments, open files, rules, docs, notes)
what: Each user turn carries structured, XML-tagged context blocks rather than free-form text.
how: Blocks built per turn include <user_query>, <attached_files> (files, code selections, terminal output and terminal selections with path and line attributes), <attached_folders> (directory trees), <documentation_context>, <open_and_recently_viewed_files> (with a note that they may be irrelevant), <agent_notes> (conversation and shared notes listing), <cursor_rules_context> (rules framed as extra documentation to use only if relevant), manually attached skills, plus <system_reminder>, <timestamp> and notification tags; summaries and recent changes can also be injected.
verevonRelevance: Verevon pages should send structured context items (typed attachments, selections, open documents) and let the runtime render the tags, so the same items work for any model.

name: Client-supplied RequestContext with progressive hydration flags
what: The client builds a large structured context object for each run and marks which parts are complete, so the first model call can start before slow facts are ready.
how: agent.v1.RequestContext carries rules, env (os_version, workspace_paths, shell, sandbox_enabled/supported, sandbox network defaults, secret_redaction_enabled, computer_use_supported, time_zone, terminals/transcripts/artifacts folders, mounted_agent_stores), repository_info, git_repos, project_layouts, mcp_instructions and file-system options, skill and plugin info, hooks_config and hooks_additional_context, custom_subagents, commit and PR attribution messages, precomputed_human_changes, permission sets from user, project and admin (auto-run), disabled_team_rules, admin_command_denylist, system_prompt_override and many *_info_complete booleans (rules, env, repository, git status, MCP, skills, custom subagents). AgentRunRequest adds client capability flags (client_supports_inline_images, preview card, prompt context usage RPC, routed model update, send_to_user).
evidence: out/vs/workbench/api/node/extensionHostProcess.js (agent.v1.RequestContext, RequestContextEnv and AgentRunRequest field lists (extracted into notes))
metric agent_client.request_context_blob.* in metric names in scratchpad/tmp/cursor-h/metrics.txt
verevonRelevance: Verevon BFF resolves instruction hierarchy server-side for chat only; a typed RequestContext sent by the page, with completeness flags, is the clean way to pass it into Do runs too (baseline: findings/t3/v-modelplane.baseline.md).

name: System prompt override and append, plus mode-specific base prompts
what: Hosts can replace or extend the system prompt, and some modes use entirely different base prompts.
how: AgentRunRequest has custom_system_prompt and system_prompt_spec (replace or append); RequestContext has system_prompt_override; the prompt generator returns a custom prompt verbatim if present, otherwise chooses per mode (Project Agent Mode has its own long prompt) and per agent identity (named persistent agents).
verevonRelevance: Org-level and app-level prompt overrides should be first-class (replace/append) fields, audited and versioned.

name: Project Agent Mode: orchestrator that only delegates and keeps a progress.md scratchpad
what: A long-horizon mode where the main agent never edits files itself, runs a phase-gated workflow through subagents and externalizes state into a durable progress file.
how: The Project Agent Mode prompt (X 61455) states hard rules: orchestrate, do not execute (all workspace changes by Task subagents), task-first for research/implementation/review, no work without clarity (use AskQuestion), a phase gate Clarify, Research, Plan, User Review, Implement, Review Panel, Iterate, Finalize, safe parallelism (never run two write-capable subagents with overlapping scope), a durable progress.md in the conversation notes folder that is regularly compacted with an archive, and a high engineering bar. Context may be condensed at any time, so state must be written to files.
verevonRelevance: This is a ready blueprint for a Verevon long-running project agent: file-based state, write-scope locking between subagents, and phase gates with a user review step.

name: Human-change awareness and read tracking in conversation state
what: The runtime tracks which files the agent has read and what the human changed since, so it can warn about stale reads or attribute edits.
how: ConversationStateStructure includes read_paths, file_states and file_states_v2, previous_workspace_uris and tracked_git_repo_branches; RequestContext includes precomputed_human_changes; metrics record read coverage; Read results include coverage telemetry.
verevonRelevance: Tracking what the agent has seen and what the user changed since lets Verevon detect conflicting edits across co-editing humans and agents.
notes: How file_states_v2 is consumed (stale-read warnings versus attribution) was not traced; medium confidence.

name: Composer headers as a table with derived columns plus JSON value
what: Conversation metadata is stored in a keyed table with indexable derived columns, while the full object is a JSON value.
how: composerHeaders rows have primary key composerId and columns workspaceId, createdAt, lastUpdatedAt, isArchived, isSubagent (task- prefixed ids or subagentInfo.parentComposerId), recency, checkpointAt, plus value JSON; a migration flag moves from a single JSON blob (allComposers) to the table; subagent conversations are separate composers excluded from search; best-of-N sub-composers are flagged.
verevonRelevance: Derived columns for list views (recency, archived, subagent, checkpoint) avoid scanning JSON; mirror in the Model Plane sessions table.

name: Post-turn labeling and follow-up classification services
what: The backend records classifications of how a turn ended and whether the next user message was a follow-up, for quality analysis.
how: aiserver.v1.InferenceService has Stream, RecordAgentFollowupClassification and RecordAgentPostTurnLabeling; ConversationsService has GetCommitMetrics; UploadLocalAgentRunToPromptQuality uploads runs for prompt-quality analysis only in the allowed privacy mode.
verevonRelevance: Closed-loop quality signals (follow-up and post-turn labels) feed model and prompt tuning; Verevon needs them as opt-in, ZDR-aware events.

name: Client telemetry stack: Statsig gates, Sentry and OpenTelemetry
what: Feature gating, crash reports and traces use standard SaaS and OTel components, switched by privacy mode.
how: Statsig SDK with 641 client-side gate names and an event proxy URL in product.json; Sentry (electron SDK and replay worker) suppressed when privacy mode is on; OpenTelemetry OTLP trace and metric exporters with auto-instrumentations packaged; enabledTelemetryLevels {error, usage}.
verevonRelevance: Flags are heavily used for rollout (agent_host_local_loop, enable_* subagents); Verevon should keep a typed flag registry owned by the Model Plane.

name: OS-level enterprise policies (ADMX) and sign-in enforcement
what: IT administrators can set policy through operating system policy mechanisms.
how: ADMX policy names include WorkspaceTrustEnabled, AllowedTeamId, SignInEnforcement, AllowedOrganizationIds, AllowedTeamIds, AllowedLoginEmails, AllowedLoginDomains, NetworkDisableHttp2, UpdateMode, ExtensionGalleryServiceUrl and AllowedExtensions; a native @anysphere/policy-watcher module reads them.
verevonRelevance: Org enforcement (allowed orgs and login domains, network protocol options) should be representable as signed policy for Verevon desktop clients as well as server-side tenancy rules.

name: Tab completion, next-edit prediction and inline edit as separate low-latency services
what: Inline features use their own services and models, not the agent loop.
how: aiserver.v1 CppService (MarkCppForEval, StreamHoldCpp, AvailableModels, RecordCppFate, AddTabRequestToEval), CursorPredictionService (CursorPredictionConfig), CmdKService (StreamCmdK, StreamHypermode, RerankCmdKContext, StreamTerminalCmdK, GetRelevantChunks), LinterService and settings cursor.cpp.disabledLanguages.
verevonRelevance: Verevon is not an IDE, but the split (agent loop versus lightweight completion services with eval hooks) shows where latency budgets differ.

name: Git worktrees as parallel agent workspaces with retention limits
what: Parallel local agents work in git worktrees that are limited in count and size and cleaned up periodically.
how: Settings cursor.worktreeMaxCount, cursor.worktreeCleanupIntervalHours and cursor.worktreesGlobalMaxSizeGb; .cursor/worktrees.json and .cursor/worktrees; the agent host createSession accepts worktreeMainPath; composer.openTerminalInWorktree command.
verevonRelevance: Worktree-per-agent with global size and age caps is the practical way to run many agents on one repo; relevant for Verevon repo-connected sandboxes.

name: Slash commands and cursor commands passed to subagents
what: User-defined commands live in files and are visible to subagents spawned by the Task tool.
how: The request context carries cursorCommands; Task spawns pass parentCursorCommands to the subagent so slash commands remain usable; plugin manifests list commands; .cursor/commands directory.
verevonRelevance: Commands propagate through subagent boundaries; Verevon should define which user-level resources a subagent inherits.

name: Distribution and updates for client runtimes
what: The product updates itself through a vendor update service and can download matching server components to remote machines.
how: updateUrl api2.cursor.sh/updates with Inno-based updater on Windows, a UpdateMode policy, and ControlService.DownloadCursorServer for remote hosts; remote server releases hosted on a blob store.
verevonRelevance: Version-matched runtime download to remote sandboxes avoids skew between UI and runtime; Verevon sandbox images should pin the runtime version.

name: Typed tool-failure taxonomy with split client-visible and model-visible messages
what: Every tool failure carries a failure type and two messages: a short generic one for the UI and an actionable one for the model.
how: Tool errors derive from a base class (gL) constructed with a failure type from a fixed enum (noop, invalid_args, unexpected_environment, user_rejected, timeout, provider_error, bad_user_device_state, aborted, exec_backend_unavailable, hook_denied, mcp_auth_error, error) plus clientVisibleErrorMessage and modelVisibleErrorMessage; for example an ambiguous replace string shows the user a generic message while the model receives the exact instruction to add context or use replace_all; failure types feed postToolUseFailure hooks and metrics; a toolExecutionTimeoutSuspension context allows pausing timeouts while waiting for approvals.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already pins a shared failure vocabulary in both loops (per the audit baseline); adding the split between what the user sees and what the model is told lets error text be actionable for the model without leaking internals to the page.
notes: Baseline reference: scratchpad/findings/t3/v-modelplane.baseline.md section 4 (tool-call retry row).

name: Parallel tool calls encouraged in descriptions and measured per invocation
what: Tool descriptions tell the model to batch independent reads, and the harness measures how many parallel calls each model invocation produced.
how: The Read description for the GPT-5-codex, codex-cloud and latest versions says it is always better to speculatively read multiple files as a batch; metrics agent.unified_handler.model_invocation.number_of_parallel_tool_calls (and the variant counting only invocations with at least one call), agent.unified_handler_number_of_tool_calls and tool_call.args.output_tokens (per tool name) quantify behaviour.
verevonRelevance: Parallelism is a prompt behaviour plus a metric, not only an executor feature; Verevon already dispatches in parallel (join_all) and should add the same measurement to tune prompts per model.

name: Entry-point aware agent behaviour (IDE, CLI, background, Slack, Linear, GitHub, API, SDK)
what: The same runtime adapts prompt, tools and final-message rules to where the request came from.
how: agentType (IDE, CLI, BACKGROUND) and backgroundAgentSource (SLACK, LINEAR, GITHUB, API, SDK) drive prompt branches: terminal-output UI differences, a rule that the last message is always shown to the user (glanceable summary, at most three paragraphs) for Linear/Slack/GitHub/API/SDK sources, Slack-specific peer-instruction handling, Slack tool names (SendSlackMessageV2, start_slack_streaming, set_slack_status), Teams and PR comment posting tools, and repoless runs that must not push or open PRs.
verevonRelevance: The Channel Plane is docs-only today; Cursor shows the minimum a channel adapter must pass into the agent: source id, final-message contract and channel-specific tool allowlist.

name: Large MCP and tool results spill to files with an outputLocation result
what: When a tool result is too large for the context it is written to disk and the model gets a pointer instead of the content.
how: The tool-result post-processor writes oversized MCP and tool output to the agent-tools directory (cap 50 MB, 40000-byte threshold) and replaces the inline content with outputLocation (path, size, lines); metrics mcp.meta.output_spill and mcp.meta.get_tools_file_output count the spills; MCP discovery payloads can also be written as files rather than inlined.
verevonRelevance: Verevon uses queryable result handles (result_query) for large MCP results; file-backed spill is the sandbox-native equivalent and works with grep and read tools.

name: Pre-final agent-store conflict barrier
what: Before an agent finishes a turn, the runtime checks whether the shared agent store changed underneath it and gives the agent a chance to reconcile.
how: When a step produced no tool call and the agent-store conflict notices flag is on, maybeInjectPreFinalConflictBarrier injects a notice (max 2 times per turn) and continues the loop instead of ending; an AGENT_STORE_CONFLICT event file and hook event name exist; ExecServerMessage.agent_store_conflict_args carries the conflict to the client.
verevonRelevance: When several agents or a human share files, a last-chance reconcile step before finishing avoids lost updates; relevant to Space co-editing.
notes: Exact trigger line approximate (barrier code sits just before the end-of-turn handling in runTurnLoop).

name: Subagent model policy and per-type model overrides
what: Which model a subagent uses is governed by policy: inherit, forced model, blocked-model checks and requires-Max checks.
how: The Task tool config evaluates subagentModelForcePolicy, forceModelId, isModelBlocked, isModelValid and requiresMaxMode against the parent requested model and parameters; AgentRunRequest carries selected_subagent_models, selected_subagent_model_details and subagent_model_overrides; custom subagents may set forceDefaultModel; the prompt lists available_subagent_models for the parent to choose from.
verevonRelevance: Per-subagent model policy (inherit, force, block) lets Verevon route cheap exploration to small models while orgs enforce allowed models.
